purpose: Start the evidence-first design phase after the implementation-valid Wave 7A.3 rejection. The next architecture must preserve the strong source-aware control while recovering complementary high-salience residual evidence; it must not treat a new salience view as a replacement for baseline coverage.

facts: The repaired candidate was implementation-valid on all 9 papers: 35 accepted anchors and 93 accepted evidence intents.
Source-aware BM25 reproduced the frozen Wave 7A.2 control at 7/13 teacher atoms.
Author-anchored BM25 recovered residual atoms e1.a and e6.a but fell to 5/13 total support and retained only 3/7 frozen control-supported atoms.
Author-anchored BGE recovered e6.a but tied its matching control at 4/13.
BM25 candidate page recall retained 100% of the coarse selected-page ceiling, so page routing is not reopened.
The valid rejection therefore localizes the residual to complementary evidence coverage: salience gains displaced established coverage rather than extending it.

coordination_boundary.rule: The ontology/semantic-control task is a downstream consumer and is not scientific authority over EXTRACT. No RDF, knowledge graph, SemanticObservation, ontology slice, or semantic-control mechanism is introduced into this design unless EXTRACT evidence independently justifies it.
coordination_boundary.future_integration: accepted EXTRACT output -> versioned provenance-bearing evidence/output adapter -> semantic-control prototype
coordination_boundary.cross_task_checkpointing: durable Git/task-capsule checkpoints and exact SHAs only; Heartbeat is liveness/ownership only

residual_reframe.old_question: Can a more salient intent generator recover the atoms missed by source-aware generation?
residual_reframe.new_question: Can a teacher-blind multi-view retrieval/selection architecture preserve the source-aware control's established coverage while adding complementary residual evidence within the unchanged top-24 proposition budget?
residual_reframe.reason: Wave 7A.3 proves that a salience view can discover complementary residuals, but standalone replacement loses strong control-supported evidence. The next independent variable is coverage-preserving composition, not another replacement prompt.

interpretation: The two valid views contain complementary evidence with a 9/13 union ceiling, so complementarity is real.
Naive concatenation, fixed branch quotas, and a simple lexical MMR sweep do not realize that union under a 24-item budget.
The first new experiment should test an explicitly coverage-oriented set objective before paying the cost and domain-risk of training a new salience classifier.
These diagnostics do not alter the valid WAVE7A3_REJECT and are not promotion evidence.

external_research_evidence.source: Pramanick et al., The Nature of NLP: Analyzing Contributions in NLP Papers, ACL 2025
evidence: NLPContributions contains nearly 2k manually annotated research-paper abstracts with contribution statements and contribution types.
The paper demonstrates a fine-tuned SciBERT contribution detector/classifier with approximately 0.80 F1, establishing that trained scientific-contribution tagging is feasible with a compact encoder.
The official repository provides Apache-2.0 training/inference code and CC-BY-SA-4.0 data but does not ship the trained checkpoint in-repository.
external_research_evidence.implication: A trained contribution/discourse detector is a credible residual-view candidate, but it requires a separate training/domain-transfer gate because the supervision is NLP-abstract-specific rather than the mixed EXTRACT corpus.

external_research_evidence.source: Lee et al., Disentangling Questions from Query Generation for Task-Adaptive Retrieval, Findings of EMNLP 2024
evidence: The paper explicitly challenges equating retrieval queries with natural-language questions.
It frames query generation as compilation of high-level search intent into task-adaptive queries and reports gains on underexplored BEIR intents.
external_research_evidence.implication: The next EXTRACT architecture should not require every evidence need to be expressed as an answer-free question; retriever-specific query compilation is a materially distinct design axis.

external_research_evidence.source: Li et al., DMQR-RAG: Diverse Multi-Query Rewriting for RAG, 2024
evidence: Different query rewrites expose different information and retrieve diverse documents.
The work also reports that more rewrites can add noise, motivating adaptive strategy selection rather than indiscriminate query multiplication.
external_research_evidence.implication: Use multiple complementary views only with a bounded selection/coverage mechanism.

external_research_evidence.source: Nair et al., A Dense Subset Index for Collective Query Coverage, ICLR 2026
evidence: The retrieval objective is a small collection whose items collectively cover query representations rather than independent top-ranked items.
The paper establishes collective coverage as a submodular objective and uses iterative selection to assemble covering sets.
external_research_evidence.implication: This directly matches the Wave 7A.3 failure mode: evidence propositions should collaborate to cover multiple atomic needs instead of competing only on one fused relevance score.

external_research_evidence.source: Nguyen and Kan, MUSS: Multilevel Subset Selection for Relevance and Diversity, UAI 2026
evidence: MUSS treats relevant-and-diverse subset selection as an explicit objective and reports RAG QA gains.
The public implementation demonstrates scalable relevance/diversity selection, but its repository license is CC BY-NC 4.0.
external_research_evidence.implication: MUSS is methodology evidence, not a production dependency. Any EXTRACT implementation should use an independently implemented bounded objective compatible with project licensing.

external_research_evidence.source: Qian et al., RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering, 2026
evidence: RVR performs retrieval, verifies a high-quality subset, then launches later retrieval conditioned on what has already been covered.
It reports improved complete recall on multi-answer retrieval, including out-of-domain gains.
external_research_evidence.implication: An iterative residual-retrieval architecture is a credible fallback family if one-shot multi-view set selection cannot preserve and extend coverage.

architecture: Keep QWEN35_SOURCE_AWARE_INTENTS_V1 as a frozen baseline view; do not replace it.
Represent an independent residual view separately rather than merging it into the baseline prompt.
Compile each view into retriever-specific probes; a probe need not be phrased as a question.
Retrieve per probe against the unchanged proposition pool.
Select the final top-24 proposition set with a teacher-blind set-level coverage objective that gives equal aggregate weight to the baseline and residual views.
Evaluate whether the selected set preserves frozen control coverage while adding residual atoms.
advantages: Directly targets the observed Wave 7A.3 displacement failure.
Can be tested first with zero new model downloads and zero new generation using already-frozen valid-run intents.
Keeps provenance, proposition pool, retrieval budget, production routing, and Qwen VERIFY unchanged.
risks: Existing residual view is itself scientifically rejected as a standalone generator and may not provide enough useful coverage.
A set objective can still over-select redundant or broad intents without a stronger residual signal.

architecture: Fine-tune or otherwise validate a compact scientific contribution/discourse classifier on public annotated scientific-text data.
Use the classifier only to identify candidate residual contribution/result/limitation/method evidence not already represented by the frozen baseline view.
Compile classifier-positive residuals into retrieval probes and feed them into the same coverage-preserving selector.
Never allow the classifier to replace exact PDF provenance or the frozen baseline coverage path.
advantages: Materially different from repeated Qwen prompt variants.
Directly implements the trained contribution/discourse direction deferred by the Wave 7A.3 contract.
Compact encoder inference is compatible with the local-first objective.
risks: NLPContributions supervision is NLP-abstract-specific and MuLMS-style argumentative zoning is domain-specific; cross-domain transfer must be measured before use.
The official NLPContributions repository does not provide a ready in-repository trained checkpoint, so training and immutable model packaging would be new work.

architecture: Run the frozen baseline retrieval first.
Use a teacher-blind local coverage verifier over selected-page propositions and the current evidence set.
Generate or compile only residual probes for uncovered evidence strata.
Run one bounded second retrieval round and select the final top-24 set.
Stop after the bounded second round; unresolved evidence remains for later Codex fallback in a future production design.
advantages: Coverage is explicit and residual-directed rather than one-shot.
Matches external comprehensive-retrieval evidence while preserving the baseline first pass.
risks: Requires a reliable definition of uncovered evidence without teacher leakage.
Adds orchestration and latency, so it should not precede the cheaper set-composition diagnostic.

rejected_or_deferred.reason: Recovered some residual atoms but displaced strong control coverage.
Did not realize the observed 9/13 union support under the fixed top-24 budget.
A fixed teacher-blind lexical MMR sweep reached at most 6/13 support in the post-hoc diagnostic.
The parallel semantic-control task is downstream coordination context, not EXTRACT scientific evidence.
The valid Wave 7A.3 result does not justify a generation-model change.
The valid Wave 7A.3 result does not reopen retriever capacity or justify trained reranking.

selected_first_diagnostic.purpose: Test only whether a teacher-blind set-level selector can preserve baseline evidence and realize complementary residual coverage from already-generated valid Wave 7A.3 views. This is an architecture-premise diagnostic, not Wave 7B and not a rerun of the rejected author-anchored generator.
inputs: exact valid Wave 7A.3 generated-intents artifact identified by hash
same nine-paper corpus and exact authoritative PDFs
same coarse top-12 selected-page proposition pool
QWEN35_SOURCE_AWARE_INTENTS_V1 accepted intents as frozen baseline view
QWEN35_AUTHOR_ANCHORED_OBLIGATIONS_V1 accepted intents as a frozen diagnostic residual view only

retrieval.reason: BM25 is the strongest frozen source-aware control at 7/13 and avoids reopening retriever capacity.

selector.candidate_pool: union of per-intent top-12 proposition rankings from the two frozen views
selector.branch_weighting: Each branch contributes exactly 0.5 total objective weight, divided uniformly across its post-guard intents.
selector.objective: F(S)=0.5/|C| * sum_{i in control} max_{p in S} r(i,p) + 0.5/|R| * sum_{i in residual} max_{p in S} r(i,p)
selector.selection: Greedy maximum marginal gain until |S|=24; deterministic proposition_id tie-break.

controls: equal-weight branch-level RRF over the two frozen top-24 lists

COMPOSITION_CONFIRMED: recovers both observed complementary residual atoms e1.a and e6.a
retains all 7/7 frozen source-aware BM25 control-supported atoms
merged-page recall is at least 90% of the frozen coarse selected-page ceiling
hard provenance and anti-leak boundaries remain intact
COMPOSITION_PARTIAL: retains at least 6/7 frozen source-aware BM25 control-supported atoms
improves total support by at least 1 atom over the frozen 7/13 control
COMPOSITION_NEGATIVE: neither CONFIRMED nor PARTIAL is met

decision_boundary.if_confirmed: Open a separate evidence-first design/training contract for FAMILY_B so a trained contribution/discourse residual detector can replace the rejected author-anchor residual proxy without changing the validated selector.
decision_boundary.if_partial: Do not train a classifier yet; inspect which baseline/residual coverage terms conflict and decide whether one bounded selector revision is evidence-justified.
decision_boundary.if_negative: Do not train a contribution classifier into the same one-shot composition architecture. Move to FAMILY_C or another materially different coverage mechanism after a new design checkpoint.

next_safe_action: CI-lock this design checkpoint only. After merge and durable task synchronization, implement the zero-generation MULTIVIEW_SUBMODULAR_COVERAGE_DIAGNOSTIC_V1 exactly as frozen here, route it through existing bounded execution authority, and run exactly one diagnostic. Do not train/download a contribution classifier, start Wave 7B, or change production EXTRACT/VERIFY before that diagnostic is checkpointed.
